audit.originality: All prompts and figures are original; mapped evidence supplies definition and recognition patterns.
audit.scope: Diffraction meaning and recognition only; gap-width-to-wavelength comparisons, interference and grating calculations are excluded.
audit.evidence: All five mapped P2 leaves were checked in whole-question context.

hints: Recall what stays fixed along the apparatus.
walkthrough: A stationary wave is indicated by repeated fixed minima or nodes and fixed maxima or antinodes; steady loops on a string are also valid.

ai_rubric.observable: States one valid stationary-wave observation such as fixed minima/nodes, fixed maxima/antinodes or steady loops

hints: Look for both spreading and a boundary feature.
walkthrough: Diffraction means spreading through a gap or around an obstacle, so B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, spreading through a gap or around an obstacle

evidence.role: Recognition of spreading after a slit.

hints: Ask whether the wave reaches new directions.
walkthrough: Spreading beyond the straight-through region is the visible sign of diffraction, so B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, wavefronts spread outside the straight-through region

hints: A doorway has edges that waves can pass around.
walkthrough: Sound spreads around the doorway edge into the listener's region, so A is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects A, sound waves spread around the doorway edge

hints: Name the behaviour, then cite gap and spreading separately.
walkthrough: The wave diffracts: it passes through a gap and the emerging fronts curve into new directions, including the geometric-shadow region beside the straight-through path.

hints: Use the name for wave spreading at a gap.
Identify the boundary feature and the changed wavefront shape.
walkthrough: The wave crosses a gap, and the outgoing curved fronts spread outside the original straight path.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies spreading or curved wavefronts reaching outside the straight-through region

hints: Look beside the straight-through region behind the barrier.
walkthrough: Curved emerging wavefronts enter the geometric-shadow region beside the straight-through path.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the wave reaches the geometric-shadow region beside the straight-through path

evidence.role: Original syllabus-based obstacle-edge extension; mapped leaves focus mainly on apertures.

hints: Explain access to the shadow region, then use the unchanged medium.
walkthrough: Diffraction spreads the wave around the edge into Y. The complete meaning is wave spreading through a gap or around an obstacle, and the obstacle branch applies here.

hints: Name the edge behaviour and where it carries the wave.
walkthrough: The wave diffracts around the obstacle edge and spreads into the geometric shadow containing Y.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the wave diffracts or spreads around the obstacle edge
Explains that spreading carries the wave into the geometric-shadow region containing Y

hints: Recall both branches of the controlled definition, then select the one shown.
walkthrough: Diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle. This diagram shows spreading around an obstacle edge.

ai_rubric.observable: States that diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle
Identifies spreading around an obstacle as the branch that applies at the shown edge

evidence.role: Diffraction definition combined with verified earlier-module superposition.

hints: Treat overlap and boundary spreading as two different jobs.
walkthrough: Panel A uses algebraic addition of displacements. Panel B is diffraction, wave spreading through a gap or around an obstacle. Superposition combines overlaps at a point; diffraction describes a boundary-driven change in directions.

hints: Recall how resultant displacement is found during overlap.
walkthrough: Use superposition: add the individual displacements algebraically.

ai_rubric.observable: States that resultant displacement is the algebraic sum of individual displacements

hints: Give the name and both branches of its definition.
walkthrough: Panel B shows diffraction, the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle.

ai_rubric.observable: States that diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle

hints: Compare what overlaps with what happens at the boundary.
walkthrough: Superposition gives the resultant when waves overlap at a point. Diffraction is spreading into new directions at a gap or obstacle edge.

ai_rubric.observable: States that superposition combines overlapping displacements at a point
States that diffraction is spreading at a gap or obstacle edge into new directions
